name: Wheat (Whole Grain)
description: Whole grain wheat is a fundamental, high-energy agricultural staple serving as a primary carbohydrate substrate for cellular metabolic fuel. By preserving the bran and germ, it provides a dense matrix of complex carbohydrates, dietary fiber, B-complex vitamins, and essential minerals crucial for bioenergetics and gastrointestinal motility.
macroIntro: A dense framework of complex carbohydrates coupled with significant plant-derived protein and minimal lipid fractions.
microIntro: A broad spectrum of micronutrients providing coenzymatic B-vitamins for the nervous system and essential metal-enzymatic minerals for cellular repair.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: High-efficiency energy base supporting muscular and cognitive output via gradual starch breakdown.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Significant plant protein (gluten fractions: gliadin/glutenin) essential for amino acid balance.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Clean lipid layer localized in the germ, rich in healthy fatty acids and Vitamin E isomers.

macroNutrients.name: Total Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Complex carbohydrate network supported by high dietary fiber (~12.2g), ensuring stable glycemic response.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
microNutrients.description: Coenzyme for pyruvate decarboxylation and ATP-energy conversion.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: Activates key metalloenzymes and supports bone matrix density.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus
microNutrients.description: Structural mineral for phospholipid membrane synthesis and cellular energy storage.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Regulates neuromuscular conduction and enzymatic glucose breakdown.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: Non-heme mineral assisting hemoglobin pool maintenance and tissue respiration.

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: Immune-modulating cofactor for DNA polymerase and tissue regeneration.

healthBenefits: Glycogen Repletion: Complex starches maintain muscle and liver glycogen without triggering insulin spikes.
Peristaltic Stimulation: High insoluble fiber content mechanically clears the GI tract and optimizes bowel movements.
Mitochondrial Support: B-vitamins catalyze Krebs cycle reactions for efficient cellular energy production.
Microbiota Prebiotic: Arabinoxylans nourish beneficial bifidobacteria and strengthen the intestinal barrier.
Antioxidant Defense: Phenolic compounds, such as ferulic acid, neutralize free radicals and protect membrane integrity.
precautionsIntro: Nutritional considerations regarding gluten, mineral absorption, and refinement:
precautions: Celiac/Gluten Sensitivity: Contains gluten (gliadin/glutenin), which triggers severe autoimmune damage in Celiac patients; strictly avoid if intolerant.
Phytic Acid Chelating: Phytic acid can inhibit iron/zinc absorption; utilize soaking, sprouting, or sourdough fermentation to neutralize.
Refinement Dangers: Modern white flour removes the bran and germ, leaving only pure starch, which elevates metabolic disease risks.
